insight_list: The deciding factor in a demon's fate is not strength but connections — White Bone Demon, the weakest (3), was killed, while Nine Spirits Primordial Sage, the strongest (10), was taken back.

Heaven's "temporary worker" mechanism — a mount descends and does evil, the owner bears no responsibility, the mount forfeits no life, and the victims get no compensation: a textbook case of "rent-seeking through power".

Dispositions form a binary structure — the backed are "taken back/recruited", the unbacked are "killed/slain", with only 4.3% demoted as a transitional category (e.g. Kui Wood Wolf stoking fires, the White Dragon Horse as a pack horse).

The Golden-Winged Roc is an extreme case of privilege in justice — after wiping out an entire nation's people in Lion Camel Kingdom, it was instead appointed a Dharma protector because it was the Buddha's kin (note: this case is not included in the 69-demon sample, but is cited separately as an extreme example of the system).
Six-Eared Macaque is a cautionary tale of "faking a backing" — having no backing, it impersonated one who did (Wukong), and was ultimately seen through and killed by the Tathāgata.
Guanyin is a "recruitment powerhouse" — Red Boy / Black Bear Demon / Inspiration King: she prefers "absorbing into the system" over "killing".
Background strength is strongly positively correlated with survival rate — background strength 9 → 100% survival, background strength 1 → 9.1% survival
